goal: Extend Docket (see docs/feature-map.md, docs/limits.md, docs/adding-a-provider.md, docs/build-prompt.md) with platform requirements shown up front, then video on every provider, a per-target video formatter, and a TikTok provider.

entries.title: 1. Requirements up front
entries.description:
Roadmap entry 1 of 8 ('Requirements up front') from .specify/roadmaps/video.md.

Before specifying, read .specify/roadmaps/video.md in full: the 'Goal' line, the 'Current state' paragraph, the rule paragraph after it, and the 'Entries, in order' list. Also read the docs it points to: docs/feature-map.md, docs/limits.md, docs/adding-a-provider.md and docs/build-prompt.md. Rules from that document: phases cannot fetch the web, so platform facts must come from docs/research/*.md, which the operator records before each entry runs. Every entry must say what it does not do and which later entry owns it. Every entry must leave the repo working.

Current state (from the document): limits live in each provider's capabilities.ts. They are enforced by validateResolvedContent and the media planner (src/server/media/variants.ts) and listed in docs/limits.md, which a doc-inventory test checks. The composer shows a per-account character counter and issues from /compose/check, but only after content breaks a rule. Many limits are marked 'interim, UNVERIFIED'.

What this entry must deliver:
- A per-account requirements summary in the composer: text limit and counting rule, image count, accepted formats, aspect range, alt text limit, media required, and text-only allowed. It is derived from capabilities and exposed through the check route or the account view, never hard-coded in UI. The document leaves the choice between check route and account view open.
- Per-platform fit badges in the media library and image picker: fits / will be converted / will be refused, per selected account. The badges use the media planner's own decisions.
- Replace the UNVERIFIED limits with researched values from docs/research and update docs/limits.md. The verification is recorded in the 'Limits verification, 2026-10-07' sections of docs/research/meta.md, docs/research/bluesky.md and docs/research/x.md. In short:
  - Instagram publish limit: the docs contradict each other (50 versus 100 per 24 h). Use 50, or read content_publishing_limit's quota_total at run time if the plan finds that cheap.
  - Instagram caption limits of 30 hashtags and 20 @mentions are new validation rules.
  - Facebook photo bytes are 10 MB, and the formats are those listed in the research. Facebook text length and photo count are still undocumented, so keep them and mark them 'UNVERIFIED (not documented by Meta, checked 2026-10-07)' rather than plain interim.
  - The X publish limit is now confirmed.
  - Also add Meta error codes 80001 and 80002 to the rate-limited set if the research says so.
- Shape the requirements model so video limits (duration, size, codec, aspect) can plug in later.

Testing: the document attaches no testing requirements to this entry. It notes only that docs/limits.md is checked by the existing doc-inventory test.

Must NOT take on: no video, no video upload, and no changes to the upload transport or upload progress UI. Entry 2 (Video groundwork) owns all of these. No new providers or post types: entries 3 to 8 own those.

Later entries (separate specs; do not implement here): 2. Video groundwork; 3. Instagram video; 4. Facebook Page video; 5. Threads video; 6. Per-target video formatter; 7. Bluesky video; 8. TikTok provider.
entries.rationale: First because it is useful on its own (people see limits before they break them) and every later entry shows its video limits through the requirements model built here. Verifying the interim limits now also means the video entries start from researched numbers.

entries.title: 2. Video groundwork
entries.description:
Roadmap entry 2 of 8 ('Video groundwork') from .specify/roadmaps/video.md.

Before specifying, read .specify/roadmaps/video.md in full: the 'Goal' line, the 'Current state' paragraph, the rule paragraph after it, and the 'Entries, in order' list. Also read the docs it points to: docs/feature-map.md, docs/limits.md, docs/adding-a-provider.md and docs/build-prompt.md. Rules from that document: phases cannot fetch the web, so platform facts must come from docs/research/*.md, which the operator records before each entry runs. Every entry must say what it does not do and which later entry owns it. Every entry must leave the repo working.

What this entry must deliver:
- Research for this entry: docs/research/upload-transport.md (browser upload transport, progress, client-side metadata) and docs/research/ffmpeg.md (ffmpeg and ffprobe in the image, licensing, commands, test fixtures). Follow their recommendations unless the plan records why not.
- MP4/MOV in the media library, with resumable or chunked upload and larger limits. The document leaves resumable-vs-chunked open and does not quantify the larger limits.
- ffprobe metadata: duration, dimensions, codecs, frame rate.
- Poster frames for thumbnails.
- ffmpeg/ffprobe in the worker image, with processing in the worker, not the web process.
- Video capability fields and validation, shown through the requirements summary from entry 1 (Requirements up front).
- The mock provider accepts video end to end.
- Document the docker-compose impact.
- Upload experience, for every upload (images too), in both the media library dropzone and the composer's media picker. Today UploadDropzone.tsx and MediaPicker.tsx send each file through a server action, one at a time, with no progress and errors only after the whole file has arrived:
  - A per-file progress bar (bytes sent / total, percent, accessible via role=progressbar and a polite live region that announces milestones, not every percent).
  - Checks in the browser before any bytes are sent: type, size and, for video, duration and dimensions read from the file's metadata. These use the same limits the server enforces (from capabilities/config, never duplicated constants). Refused files show the reason at once.
  - Errors as they happen: a network drop, a server refusal or a storage failure mid-upload shows on that file's row immediately, with Retry (resuming where it stopped when the transport supports it) and Cancel.
  - After upload, a processing state per file (probing, making the poster frame) that updates until the item is ready or failed, without a page reload.
  - Several files may upload in parallel with a small concurrency cap; one failure never hides or stops the others.
  - The transport for large files (presigned multipart upload straight to the bucket, tus, or chunked uploads through the app) is decided in plan/research, given that the bucket is S3-compatible (R2, S3, MinIO; see docs/storage.md) and must work behind the documented reverse proxies.

Testing: the mock provider accepts video end to end. Upload tests cover progress reporting, a mid-upload failure with retry, the in-browser refusal using the server's limits, and the processing state reaching ready and failed.

Must NOT take on: no real provider publishes video yet. Real-provider video belongs to entry 3 (Instagram), 4 (Facebook Page), 5 (Threads), 7 (Bluesky) and 8 (TikTok). No transcoding, cropping or trimming for each target: entry 6 owns it. Here an out-of-range video is reported by validation, not fixed.

Later entries (separate specs; do not implement here): 3. Instagram video; 4. Facebook Page video; 5. Threads video; 6. Per-target video formatter; 7. Bluesky video; 8. TikTok provider.
entries.rationale: Every video entry needs video in the media library, ffprobe/ffmpeg in the worker, video capability fields and a usable upload experience for large files. Proving it with the mock provider keeps platform quirks out of the base layer.

entries.title: 3. Instagram video
entries.description:
Roadmap entry 3 of 8 ('Instagram video') from .specify/roadmaps/video.md.

Before specifying, read .specify/roadmaps/video.md in full: the 'Goal' line, the 'Current state' paragraph, the rule paragraph after it, and the 'Entries, in order' list. Read entries 1 and 2 especially, since this entry builds on the requirements summary and the video groundwork. Also read the docs it points to: docs/feature-map.md, docs/limits.md, docs/adding-a-provider.md and docs/build-prompt.md. Rules from that document: phases cannot fetch the web, so Instagram facts must come from the operator's research in docs/research/ (Meta research lives in docs/research/meta.md). Every entry must say what it does not do and which later entry owns it. Every entry must leave the repo working.

Research for this entry: docs/research/meta-video.md (Instagram section). Key facts: media_type=VIDEO was removed for single videos in 2023, so 'feed video' means a Reel with share_to_feed=true, not a separate media type. Other facts there: the 400 containers per 24 h cap, status polling once a minute for up to 5 minutes, and the Reel specs.

What this entry must deliver:
- Reels (media_type=REELS).
- Feed video, as a Reel with share_to_feed=true.
- Mixed image/video carousels. Reels are not allowed in carousels.
- Container status polling through the existing step machine.
- The composer lets the person choose Reel or feed video for a single-video Instagram target, and the requirements summary shows the limits for the chosen type.

Testing: step-machine tests for each new path (REELS, VIDEO, mixed carousel), including polling until FINISHED, an ERROR container, and timeouts. Mocked Graph tests in the style of the existing Instagram publish tests.

Must NOT take on: Stories, which are not on this roadmap. Cropping, padding or trimming video to fit Instagram: entry 6 owns that, so here out-of-range video is refused by validation with a clear message. Facebook (entry 4) and Threads (entry 5).

Later entries (separate specs; do not implement here): 4. Facebook Page video; 5. Threads video; 6. Per-target video formatter; 7. Bluesky video; 8. TikTok provider.
entries.rationale: Instagram video reuses the container-and-poll flow that image posts already use, so it is the cheapest real provider to prove video publishing on.

entries.title: 4. Facebook Page video
entries.description:
Roadmap entry 4 of 8 ('Facebook Page video') from .specify/roadmaps/video.md.

Before specifying, read .specify/roadmaps/video.md in full: the 'Goal' line, the 'Current state' paragraph, the rule paragraph after it, and the 'Entries, in order' list. Read entries 1 and 2 especially, since this entry builds on the requirements summary and the video groundwork. Also read the docs it points to: docs/feature-map.md, docs/limits.md, docs/adding-a-provider.md and docs/build-prompt.md. Rules from that document: phases cannot fetch the web, so Facebook facts must come from the operator's research in docs/research/ (Meta research lives in docs/research/meta.md). Every entry must say what it does not do and which later entry owns it. Every entry must leave the repo working.

Research for this entry: docs/research/meta-video.md (Facebook section). It covers Reels at 3 to 90 s and 9:16, the cap of 30 API-published reels per 24 h, the rupload flow, and the gaps that are still unverified.

What this entry must deliver:
- Page Reels via the Reels Publishing API: start, upload to rupload.facebook.com, finish with video_state=PUBLISHED, then status polling.
- Page video posts.

Testing: step-machine tests for each upload phase and polling, including a failed or stuck upload, with mocked Graph and rupload calls.

Must NOT take on: Facebook Stories, and mixing video with images in one Facebook post. Cropping or trimming to fit (entry 6). Threads (entry 5).

Later entries (separate specs; do not implement here): 5. Threads video; 6. Per-target video formatter; 7. Bluesky video; 8. TikTok provider.
entries.rationale: Shares the Meta app and tokens with Instagram, but needs its own three-phase upload. Instagram goes first so the base layer is already proven on a real platform.

entries.title: 5. Threads video
entries.description:
Roadmap entry 5 of 8 ('Threads video') from .specify/roadmaps/video.md.

Before specifying, read .specify/roadmaps/video.md in full: the 'Goal' line, the 'Current state' paragraph, the rule paragraph after it, and the 'Entries, in order' list. Read entries 1 and 2 especially, since this entry builds on the requirements summary and the video groundwork. Also read the docs it points to: docs/feature-map.md, docs/limits.md, docs/adding-a-provider.md and docs/build-prompt.md. Rules from that document: phases cannot fetch the web, so Threads facts must come from the operator's research in docs/research/ (Meta research lives in docs/research/meta.md). Every entry must say what it does not do and which later entry owns it. Every entry must leave the repo working.

Research for this entry: docs/research/meta-video.md (Threads section). It covers video up to 300 s and 1 GB, carousels of 2 to 20 items, and reading fields=status,error_message when polling.

What this entry must deliver:
- media_type=VIDEO posts.
- Video items in carousels.

Testing: step-machine tests for VIDEO and a mixed carousel, including container polling and failure, with mocked Threads API calls.

Must NOT take on: cropping or trimming to fit (entry 6).

Later entries (separate specs; do not implement here): 6. Per-target video formatter; 7. Bluesky video; 8. TikTok provider.
entries.rationale: Same container pattern as Instagram, so it lands quickly once entry 3 has proven it.

entries.title: 6. Per-target video formatter
entries.description:
Roadmap entry 6 of 8 ('Per-target video formatter') from .specify/roadmaps/video.md.

Before specifying, read .specify/roadmaps/video.md in full: the 'Goal' line, the 'Current state' paragraph, the rule paragraph after it, and the 'Entries, in order' list. Read entry 2 especially, since it puts ffmpeg/ffprobe, poster frames and video processing in the worker. Also read the docs it points to: docs/feature-map.md, docs/limits.md, docs/adding-a-provider.md and docs/build-prompt.md, plus the image media planner (src/server/media/variants.ts). Rules from that document: phases cannot fetch the web, so per-platform video limits must come from docs/research/*.md, which the operator records before each entry runs. Every entry must say what it does not do and which later entry owns it. Every entry must leave the repo working.

What this entry must deliver, in the worker:
- Crop with a focal point the person sets on the poster frame, or pad (blurred copy or solid colour).
- Trim to a start/end within each platform's maximum duration.
- H.264/AAC MP4 encode within each target's bitrate, frame rate and size limits.
- A low-resolution preview per target before publishing.
- Use the same per-target variant pattern as the image planner.
- Applies to every provider that publishes video when this entry runs (mock, Instagram, Facebook, Threads). Later providers get it by declaring capabilities.

Testing: unit tests that build the ffmpeg filter chain for crop, pad and trim; worker tests on small fixture clips that check the output's dimensions, duration and codecs with ffprobe; a test that a video already within a target's limits is passed through, not re-encoded.

Must NOT take on: burned-in captions, smart crop that tracks subjects, and per-platform cover-frame choice; none of these is on this roadmap. Bluesky (entry 7) and TikTok (entry 8).

Later entries (separate specs; do not implement here): 7. Bluesky video; 8. TikTok provider.
entries.rationale: Comes after the three Meta providers so it fits real, researched limits for working targets rather than guesses. It still comes before Bluesky and TikTok, whose tighter duration and size limits make trimming and re-encoding necessary in practice.

entries.title: 7. Bluesky video
entries.description:
Roadmap entry 7 of 8 ('Bluesky video') from .specify/roadmaps/video.md.

Before specifying, read .specify/roadmaps/video.md in full: the 'Goal' line, the 'Current state' paragraph, the rule paragraph after it, and the 'Entries, in order' list. Read entries 1, 2 and 6 especially, since this entry builds on the requirements summary, the video groundwork and the per-target video formatter. Also read the docs it points to: docs/feature-map.md, docs/limits.md, docs/adding-a-provider.md and docs/build-prompt.md. Rules from that document: phases cannot fetch the web, so Bluesky facts must come from the operator's research in docs/research/ (Bluesky research lives in docs/research/bluesky.md). Every entry must say what it does not do and which later entry owns it. Every entry must leave the repo working.

Research for this entry: docs/research/bluesky-video.md.
- Limits: MP4 only, 300,000,000 bytes, and about 25 videos or 10 GB per day; check getUploadLimits.
- Duration is unverified, so use the conservative product limit the research gives.
- Upload flow: a service auth token from the PDS, then upload to video.bsky.app, then poll getJobStatus.
- @atproto/api does not mint the service token or call video.bsky.app, so Docket must do both.

What this entry must deliver:
- app.bsky.embed.video upload through the video service.
- Job polling.
- Bluesky's video limits declared in capabilities, so entry 6's formatter trims and encodes for Bluesky.

Testing: step-machine tests for upload, job polling, job failure and publish, with mocked XRPC calls.

Must NOT take on: TikTok (entry 8).

Later entries (separate specs; do not implement here): 8. TikTok provider.
entries.rationale: Bluesky's short maximum duration and small size limit make it rely on entry 6's trim and encode, so it comes after the formatter.

entries.title: 8. TikTok provider
entries.description:
Roadmap entry 8 of 8 ('TikTok provider') from .specify/roadmaps/video.md.

Before specifying, read .specify/roadmaps/video.md in full: the 'Goal' line, the 'Current state' paragraph, the rule paragraph after it, and the 'Entries, in order' list. Read entries 1, 2 and 6 especially, since this entry builds on the requirements summary, the video groundwork and the per-target video formatter. Also read the docs it points to: docs/feature-map.md, docs/limits.md, docs/adding-a-provider.md (how to add a provider) and docs/build-prompt.md, plus docs/meta-setup.md as the model for the setup doc. Rules from that document: phases cannot fetch the web, so TikTok facts must come from the operator's research in docs/research/, recorded before this entry runs. Every entry must say what it does not do and which later entry owns it. Every entry must leave the repo working.

Research for this entry: docs/research/tiktok.md. Read its blockers section first.
- Each deployer registers and audits their own TikTok app. Unaudited apps are limited to SELF_ONLY posts and 5 users per 24 h.
- Photo posts are PULL_FROM_URL only and need a verified domain or URL prefix. The setup doc must explain this; it may need a custom bucket domain.
- Video should use FILE_UPLOAD, in 5 to 64 MB chunks, uploaded in order.
- The redirect URI must be https.
- Access tokens last 24 h, refresh tokens 365 d, and refresh tokens rotate.
- Store publish_id as the external id.
- TikTok requires express consent and a creator-info-driven UI at send time. It is UNVERIFIED whether consent captured at scheduling passes audit. The spec must record this risk and capture consent explicitly when the post is scheduled, with the creator info re-checked at publish. If creator info changed so that the chosen privacy is no longer allowed, the post fails clearly instead of posting.

What this entry must deliver:
- A new provider folder.
- OAuth connect.
- Content Posting API direct post for video and photo posts.
- TikTok's required posting UI fields: a privacy picker from creator info, and interaction toggles.
- Unaudited-app behaviour (posts forced to SELF_ONLY), surfaced clearly in the UI and docs.
- A setup doc like docs/meta-setup.md.

Testing: mocked OAuth and Content Posting API tests (init, upload or PULL_FROM_URL, status polling, failure), and a test that an unaudited app's post is shown as private in the UI. No live check is owed until the operator's app is audited.

Must NOT take on: getting the app through TikTok's audit, which is the operator's job (the doc explains how). Analytics, comments and inbox. It is the last entry in the roadmap.
entries.rationale: A whole new provider with its own OAuth app and an audit outside our control. Last, so it inherits the requirements summary, video groundwork and formatter. Owner note: start the TikTok developer app and audit early.
